profile.reading:
CloudHQ LC3 sits at 44631 Waxpool Road, Ashburn, Virginia, one of fourteen numbered buildings on CloudHQ's LC Campus. Unlike most of the other LC-numbered buildings, LC3 is individually and specifically named on CloudHQ's current LC Campus page as one of two buildings, alongside LC4, actively under construction, with the company stating a "Ready for Service within 20 months" timeline for that new capacity as of this session's retrieval. CloudHQ's own campus page places the site directly off Loudoun County Parkway "in the heart of Ashburn," describing it as sitting amid "the densest concentration of fiber in the world." CloudHQ states the full LC Campus totals roughly 8.5 million square feet and 1,256 megawatts of total critical IT load across its fourteen data centers, with 756 megawatts currently available; this is a campus-wide total not broken out by individual building. CloudHQ was founded in 2016 by Hossein Fateh, who also founded QTS Realty Trust and, per CloudHQ's own materials, was the first person in the United States to obtain an IRS ruling allowing data center income to qualify for real estate investment trust tax treatment. CloudHQ is privately held through the Fateh Family Office, with regional headquarters in Washington DC, London, and Singapore, and states a company-wide net-zero emissions target by 2040. CloudHQ does not name a power utility for the LC Campus on its current site; Dominion Energy is the dominant electric utility across Loudoun County as a matter of public record, though this is not independently confirmed for CloudHQ specifically.

CloudHQ's "campus within a campus" marketing concept at LC allows customers to take multiple LC-numbered buildings as one contiguous deployment, a positioning particularly relevant to LC3 and LC4 as the two buildings currently under active construction and leasing. CloudHQ's global portfolio spans 23 campuses and more than 30 million square feet across six countries, with more than 1,380 megawatts of critical IT load already contracted company-wide, and trade press has separately reported CloudHQ planning a 4-million-square-foot expansion campus in Ashburn beyond the LC Campus's existing 8.5 million square foot footprint.

reading.body:
CloudHQ LC3 in Ashburn, Virginia is a single building within a fourteen-facility campus totaling 1,256 MW of critical IT load, but the operator does not publish power consumption at the individual building level.

The LC Campus sits in the densest data center cluster in North America, where power availability and real estate directly constrain capacity. CloudHQ's parent company was built by an operator who has constructed and managed over 700 MW across his career, indicating capital and expertise focused on the infrastructure layer itself. The 756 MW of available critical load across the campus demonstrates that even in Ashburn, expansion potential depends on grid connection and power delivery rather than floor space alone. The 8.5 million square feet across fourteen buildings shows the footprint required to house this density.

This data does not reveal LC3's individual power draw, operational status, customer occupancy, or power source mix. It does not address whether the campus operates at full capacity or sits partially vacant. The neighboring LC2 building shares the same street address prefix, suggesting a campus design where buildings are close enough for shared infrastructure, but individual building metrics remain opaque to outside observers. Without facility-level power data, only CloudHQ's aggregate portfolio statement can guide estimates of this site's role in regional power demand.
